newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW seeking to raise U.S. vehicle sales.
newsitem.headline: BMW seeking to raise U.S. vehicle sales.

text.p: BMW AG hopes to deliver about 110,000 vehicles to customers in the United States this year, up from 105,800 in 1996, a spokesman said Tuesday.
The spokesman confirmed comments by BMW's new top executive in the United States, Henrich Heitmann, that the German automaker was seeking to strengthen its presence in the North American market.
Heitmann made the comments to the industry magazine PS Report. He was also quoted as saying that about 50 percent of BMW's business in the United States was in vehicle leasing.
He added that BMW was against developing its own sport utility vehicle and would instead rely on the Land Rover and Range Rover models developed by BMW unit Rover of Britain.
Heitmann's comments came as BMW on Monday said July U.S. car sales were flat at 10,769 models but that sales for the first seven months of the year rose 21 percent to 73,170 vehicles.
